purpose: First visual occurrence and directional twilight photometry from one 1990 at-sea session; transcribed from original Japanese journal page images, not secondary abstract.

original_publication.title: An Experimental Study on the Extent of the Visible Horizon in the Duration of Twilight
original_publication.japanese_title: 薄明時の水平線の見え方について
original_publication.journal: The Journal of Japan Institute of Navigation
original_publication.source_custody_note: Official publisher original Japanese scanned PDF page images visually inspected. No original PDF byte hash, underlying instrument files, or ship log was acquired.

observation_session.position_printed: 36 deg 16.2 min S; 178 deg 09.2 min E (South Pacific, moving vessel)
observation_session.sunset_clock_printed: 18:56 (zone and clock relation to UTC unspecified)
observation_session.sensor_for_directional_sky_luminance: TOPCON BM-8 luminance meter, stated measurement range 0.01 to 12,000,000 cd/m2
observation_session.sensor_for_whole_sky_illuminance: MINOLTA T-1M illuminance meter, stated range 0.01 to 300,000 lx
observation_session.sky_grid: Solar-set azimuth 257deg is reference 0; relative azimuths 0/45/90/135/180 degrees; elevations 10/30/50/70/90 degrees, plus horizon vicinity +/-2deg; sequence across directions about 100 seconds, estimated solar-altitude drift about 0.3deg.
observation_session.sun_altitude_method: Derived by paper authors from approximate 90-minute sunset-to-18deg twilight duration; not an independently timestamped high-precision ephemeris.

transcription_qualifications: Tab.5 heading indicates star/planet initial visual recognition and background luminance. Values are printed original-paper tabular entries, not newly measured by this project.
Solar-center angles are approximate figure/text milestones, not individually UTC time-stamped event rows; a single ship sunset 18:56 is NOT a first-sighting time.
The paper's luminance tabulation comes from a sampled multi-angle sky field; do NOT equate it with a synchronous calibrated star-pointing radiance spectrum at the instant of subjective detection.
The relative azimuth uses the printed sunset bearing as the zero reference; do not silently treat it as absolute azimuth or exact Sun-star angular separation.
Sky directions were sampled in sequence over ~100 s; the paper itself notes ~0.3deg solar change during the sweep. Do NOT claim timing precision from the printed figures.
The author weather code and Moon age are NOT calibrated cloud fraction/AOD aerosol profile, moon radiance, or eye-adaptation state.
The photopic cd/m2 values are sky luminance, not star brightness or mag/arcsec2; 0/detection-floor values in Table 2 MUST NOT be treated as physical zero.
All values are historical nonblinded already-seen published outcomes; do NOT rebrand as an unseen independent prospective validation holdout.
next_source_gate: Seek ship log/clock UTC offset, raw observer per-object first YES/last NO, original photometer timestamp/direction/calibration files, independent atmosphere/cloud/AOD and observer vision protocol; else retain as source-bounded historic context / possible directional radiance comparison only.
safety: No protected Taylor/Ann Arbor/Jerusalem, MYSTIC ordinals67/68, scientific dispatch, prediction lock, paid service, merge, or production release. Published observations seen before analysis; do not fit or call independent.
